title: Calli Hauger-Thackery Wins Honolulu and Houston
excerpt: Calli Hauger-Thackery won Honolulu on Dec 14, 2025, then Houston four weeks later in 2:24:17. What it does and doesn't mean for your recovery.
body:
Britain's Calli Hauger-Thackery won the Honolulu Marathon on December 14, 2025, in 2:30:43 in rainy conditions, becoming the first British woman to win the race. Four weeks later, on January 11, 2026, she won the Houston Marathon in 2:24:17, ahead of Sara Hall (2:26:26).

Two marathon wins in four weeks is unusual even for a professional, and it shouldn't be read as a recovery schedule for most runners. What it does show is that recovery is individual, and that it depends on how hard the first race was and how well you recover from it.

After your next marathon, judge your return to training by how you respond rather than by a fixed date. Track your sleep, your morning resting heart rate and how your legs feel on easy runs. Those signals are better guides than a calendar.

Sources: LetsRun.com; Athletics Weekly
keyTakeaway: Recovery is individual: judge readiness by how you feel and recover, not by a fixed calendar.
